name: Sub-agents
description: Delegation: spawn background minimal-agent workers, steer them, review their work, fold results back. A worker is a real headless agent process with its own session id. A 1s heartbeat supervises it: it reaps exits, paints a live fleet widget, and injects each finished worker's distilled result between turns. State lives at ~/.minimal-agent/sessions/<leadSid>.subagents.jsonl. Disable with MINIMAL_AGENT_DISABLE_SUBAGENTS=1.

tool.name: SpawnAgent
tool.description: Delegate one self-contained unit of work to a background sub-agent. Use it when the unit floods your context, or when it is genuinely independent of the other work. Do not use it for a quick edit you can do yourself, or for work that needs constant back-and-forth. Returns the worker id, its label and its isolation tier. A one line digest arrives between turns.

task.description: The delegation prompt: a clear objective, the scope/file boundaries the worker must stay inside, and the exact output you want back. The single biggest lever on whether delegation succeeds. Required.

agent.description: Named specialist: explorer (files), planner (a plan), worker (edits), reviewer (issues), integrator (gate, commit), log-miner (log findings). Omit to use `system`.

system.description: Inline system prompt defining the worker's role, used when `agent` is omitted. Folded above the task.

model.description: Optional model id for the worker. When omitted, the worker inherits the model YOU the lead are running, for both named specialists and inline workers. Delegating does not downgrade your model. (Opt into per-role models, cheap scout and flagship deep, by setting MINIMAL_AGENT_SUBAGENT_AUTO_TIER=1. Even then an explicit model here still wins.) Pass `model` when you want a specific model for one spawn. Accepts any model id your provider exposes. An unknown id makes the worker crash at startup, which surfaces as a `failed` handle with the real error.

effort.description: Optional reasoning effort for the worker. Only pass a value the target model accepts (check ModelInfo for the lead/worker model: effort.levels). Do not invent levels from a universal menu: models differ (e.g. some accept low/medium/high, others medium/high/max only). Prefer omitting effort so the model default applies. That is safer than guessing. An unsupported value fails the spawn (or used to crash the child at boot).

isolation.description: Context tier. `fresh` (default): a clean context with only the task plus the worker's system prompt, for maximum context compression. `fork`: inherit this conversation's full history (shares the prompt cache, sees your context) for a side task that needs the background without re-explaining.

label.description: Short display name for the worker in the fleet widget. Defaults to the agent type.

taskId.description: Link this worker to a task from the Task tool using its canonical id, such as `1` or `1a`. When the worker finishes the linked todo is ticked done automatically (or canceled with a reason if the worker fails). Use it to make a worker own one of your todos.

expectArtifacts.description: Absolute paths this worker must produce to count as done. When set, the supervisor refuses to mark the worker done unless every path exists and is non-empty, and a missing one flips it to 'incomplete' with a warning. Use for delegations whose whole point is to produce a file (e.g. ['/abs/findings.md']) so the system enforces the deliverable instead of you having to check. The worker receives the list. Read-only types (explorer, planner, reviewer, log-miner) deliver the files through ReportResult `deliverables`.

budget.description: Optional runtime budget. The supervisor stops a worker that exceeds it.

maxTurns.description: Max model responses. The worker is stopped when it starts one more.

maxTokens.description: Max generated tokens (output, thinking included) summed over the run. The worker is stopped past it.

tool.name: ReportResult
tool.description: Record a sub-agent result for the lead as the final action of a worker session. Use it when the unit is complete and you must hand the finding back. Do not use it as the lead: the lead reads the record with SubAgentsAgentResult. Pass required files in `deliverables` and the tool writes them. Returns the stored result, the artifact list and the incomplete flag. It refuses to finish while a required file is missing, unless incomplete is true.

summary.description: Your findings: a dense, self-contained synthesis the lead will read. Not a pointer to a file, the actual content.

artifacts.description: Absolute paths of files you created or changed, if any.

incomplete.description: Set true if you could not finish the task. The lead will treat the work as unverified and may re-spawn. Default false.

deliverables.description: Files the lead required (expectArtifacts). The tool writes each one for you, also in read-only mode. Only the required paths are allowed.

path.description: Absolute path of one required file.

content.description: The full file text. Must not be empty.

tool.name: ListAgents
tool.description: List this session's sub-agents at a glance. Use it to see the fleet before you pull a result or stop a worker. Do not use it for one worker in depth: use SubAgentsAgentStatus. It pulls no worker transcript. Returns the id, type, status, elapsed time, tokens and current activity of each sub-agent.

tool.name: AgentStatus
tool.description: Show the status of one sub-agent, or of the whole fleet when you give no id. Use it to check progress, model, isolation tier and linked session. Do not use it to read a result: use SubAgentsAgentResult. Do not use it to read activity: use SubAgentsAgentOutput. Returns a status text with no transcript.

id.description: The sub-agent handle (e.g. A2). Omit for the whole fleet.

tool.name: AgentResult
tool.description: Pull the distilled deliverable of a finished sub-agent into your context. Use it after a worker reaches `done`. This is the only sub-agent tool that carries real worker content back. Do not use it to watch a running worker: use SubAgentsAgentOutput. Returns the result summary and artifact references, not the full transcript. The text is bounded.

tool.name: AgentOutput
tool.description: Tail the recent activity of one sub-agent: its latest tool calls and notes with timestamps. Use it to see what a worker does right now. Use it sparingly, because the fleet widget and the digest usually suffice. Do not use it to read a final result: use SubAgentsAgentResult. Returns a bounded activity text, never the whole transcript.

tool.name: Mailbox
tool.description: Post and read short notes on a shared board between sibling sub-agents and the lead. Use it only when your task tells you to coordinate, to claim a file, flag a blocker or hand off a finding. Do not use it for general talk. Returns the posted note, or the notes addressed to you after a `since` cursor.

action.description: post a message, or read your messages. Default read.

to.description: Recipient: a worker id (e.g. A3) or "*" for broadcast. Default broadcast. (post only)

kind.description: Short category: note | claim | blocker | handoff. Default note. (post only)

body.description: The message text. Required for post.

since.description: ISO timestamp cursor: read only messages newer than this. (read only)

tool.name: StopAgent
tool.description: Cancel a running sub-agent by id. This signals its process and marks it stopped. Use it when a worker is no longer needed, was superseded or goes off track. Do not use it to read a result: use SubAgentsAgentResult. Returns a line that names the stopped sub-agent and the reason, if you gave one. An unknown id returns an error.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded on the handle.
